questions.enonce_markdown: Two events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A) = \dfrac25$, $P(A\cup B) = \dfrac{7}{10}$. Find $P(B)$, if $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive.
questions.corrige_markdown:
If $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive then $P(A\cap B) = 0$, so by the addition law $P(A\cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A\cap B) = P(A) + P(B)$:

$$P(B) = \frac{7}{10} - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{7}{10} - \frac{4}{10} = \frac{3}{10}$$

**$P(B) = \dfrac{3}{10}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Two events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A) = \dfrac25$, $P(A\cup B) = \dfrac{7}{10}$. Find $P(B)$, if $A$ and $B$ are independent.
questions.corrige_markdown:
If $A$ and $B$ are independent then $P(A\cap B) = P(A)P(B)$. The addition law gives

$$P(A\cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A)P(B) \;\Rightarrow\; \frac{7}{10} = \frac25 + P(B)\left(1 - \frac25\right) = \frac25 + \frac35 P(B)$$

$$\frac35 P(B) = \frac{7}{10} - \frac{4}{10} = \frac{3}{10} \;\Rightarrow\; P(B) = \frac{3}{10}\times\frac53 = \frac12$$

**Check:** $P(A\cap B) = \tfrac25\times\tfrac12 = \tfrac15$ and $\tfrac25 + \tfrac12 - \tfrac15 = \tfrac{4 + 5 - 2}{10} = \tfrac{7}{10}$.

**$P(B) = \dfrac12$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When a contractor needs a truck, it could be hired from one of three companies $X$, $Y$ or $Z$. Of the trucks hired $40\%$ are from $X$, $50\%$ from $Y$ and $10\%$ from $Z$. $9\%$ of trucks hired from $X$, $6\%$ of trucks hired from $Y$ and $20\%$ of trucks hired from $Z$ all arrived late at the contractor's estate. A truck is hired at random from a company. Calculate the probability that the truck will arrive late.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $L$ be the event "the truck arrives late". The events $X$, $Y$, $Z$ are exclusive and exhaustive ($0.4 + 0.5 + 0.1 = 1$), so the law of total probability applies. (Tree diagram: first branches to $X, Y, Z$ with probabilities $0.4, 0.5, 0.1$; each then splits into late with $0.09$, $0.06$, $0.20$ and not late.)

$$P(L) = P(X)P(L\mid X) + P(Y)P(L\mid Y) + P(Z)P(L\mid Z)$$

$$P(L) = 0.4\times 0.09 + 0.5\times 0.06 + 0.1\times 0.20 = 0.036 + 0.030 + 0.020 = 0.086$$

**$P(\text{late}) = 0.086$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: With the same set-up (trucks hired from $X$, $Y$, $Z$ with probabilities $0.4$, $0.5$, $0.1$; probability of arriving late $9\%$, $6\%$, $20\%$ respectively), calculate the probability that a truck hired at random will not arrive late.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Arriving late and not arriving late are complementary events:

$$P(L') = 1 - P(L) = 1 - 0.086 = 0.914$$

**Check** by direct summation: $0.4\times 0.91 + 0.5\times 0.94 + 0.1\times 0.80 = 0.364 + 0.470 + 0.080 = 0.914$.

**$P(\text{not late}) = 0.914$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: With the same set-up (trucks hired from $X$, $Y$, $Z$ with probabilities $0.4$, $0.5$, $0.1$; probability of arriving late $9\%$, $6\%$, $20\%$ respectively), given that a truck hired arrives late, find the probability that it comes from $Y$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
This is a conditional probability (Bayes' theorem):

$$P(Y\mid L) = \frac{P(Y\cap L)}{P(L)} = \frac{P(Y)P(L\mid Y)}{P(L)} = \frac{0.5\times 0.06}{0.086} = \frac{0.030}{0.086} = \frac{15}{43}\approx 0.349$$

**$P(Y\mid L) = \dfrac{15}{43}\approx 0.349$.**
